examples.en: The ball hit the wall and bounced back.
I flicked the marble with my finger.
If you pluck a guitar string, it makes a sound.
The stone skipped across the water.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 일부러 튕기는 것 같아요.
examples.en: She seems to be playing hard to get on purpose.
Raindrops bounced off the umbrella and wet my clothes.

explain: '튀다'와 비슷하지만 '튕기다'는 손가락이나 줄을 세게 쳐서 퉁 하고 움직이게 할 때도 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 관심 있으면서도 일부러 쉽게 받아 주지 않는 모습을 말해요.

phrases.en: play hard to get
phrases.nuance_ko: 관심이 있어도 일부러 바로 받아 주지 않는 모습을 말하는 구어체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Colloquial: refusing or delaying on purpose despite being interested.

explain_en: An object bounces off a surface, or flicking something with a finger. Similar to 튀다, but 튕기다 also covers flicking a finger or plucking a string. Said of a person, it means acting hard to get on purpose even though they are interested.

examples.en: The plan is given up halfway.
That business was finally abandoned.
I took out a dream that had been given up.

examples.ko: 시간이 없으면 일부는 포기될 수 있어요.
examples.en: If time is short, some may be given up.
Several plans are being dropped.
The construction was dropped, so the land is empty.

explain: 계획, 사업, 공사처럼 하던 일이 끝까지 가지 못하고 멈췄을 때 써요. 사람이 스스로 그만두는 건 '포기하다'예요. 일이 멈췄다는 뜻으로 '중단되다'도 많이 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '포기하다'를 훨씬 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The construction was stopped because of the rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 멈췄다는 뜻이고, 다시 시작할 수도 있어서 '포기되다'보다 약해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the work stopped, and it may restart, so it is weaker than 포기되다.

phrases.en: That plan hasn't been given up yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계속 이어지고 있다는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form meaning it is still continuing.

phrases.en: My friend gave up halfway.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 주어일 때 쓰고 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person is the subject, and much more common in daily talk.

explain_en: Used when a plan, business or construction project stops before it is finished. A person quitting by choice uses the active verb. The verb for 'be suspended' is also common for stopped projects. In daily talk the active verb is far more common.

examples.en: The enemy army finally declared surrender.
Okay, I give up. I lost.
When his strength ran out, he surrendered.
The news of the surrender was broadcast on the radio.
My sibling could not stand the tickling and gave in.
We will not surrender to the end.

explain: '항복하다'로 동사처럼 쓰고, 장난으로 "항복!"이라고 외치기도 해요. 비슷한 '굴복하다'는 힘이나 압력에 눌려 따르는 거고, '항복'은 싸움이나 승부에서 졌다고 인정하는 거예요.

phrases.en: He finally surrendered.
phrases.nuance_ko: '항복'을 동사로 쓸 때의 기본 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic verb form of 항복.

phrases.en: The general accepted the enemy's surrender.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이긴 쪽에서 상대의 항복을 받아들일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the winning side accepting surrender.

phrases.en: It's too hard, so I give up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가볍게 졌다고 말할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also be used lightly to admit defeat.

explain_en: Admitting defeat in a fight, war or game (항복을 선언하다) It is used as a verb with '하다' ('항복하다'), and people also shout '항복!' as a joke when they give up. The similar '굴복하다' (yield) is about bowing to power or pressure, while '항복' is about admitting defeat in a fight or contest.

en: to be possessed; to be bewitched; to be lured

examples.en: I was completely spellbound by that singer's voice.

examples.ko: 저는 뭐에 홀린 것처럼 가게에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: I walked into the shop as if I were under a spell.

examples.ko: 예쁜 광고에 홀려서 비싼 가방을 샀어요.
examples.en: I got lured by a pretty ad and bought an expensive bag.
People stared as if they were entranced by the magic.
Don't let yourself be taken in by sweet words.
Anyone would be charmed by that actor's smile.

explain: 홀리다는 무엇에 마음을 빼앗겨 정신을 못 차리는 모습이에요. '뭐에 홀린 것 같다'는 이유를 모르겠는데 이상하게 끌려갔을 때 자주 해요. '반하다'가 좋아하는 마음이라면 홀리다는 정신이 나간 듯한 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.example: 제가 왜 그걸 샀는지 모르겠어요. 뭐에 홀린 것 같아요.
phrases.en: I feel like I was possessed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기가 한 행동이 이해되지 않을 때 쓰는 말이에요. 귀신이 씐 것처럼 정신이 없었다는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said when you cannot understand your own action, as if something took control of you.
phrases.en_equiv: I don't know what came over me.

explain_en: 홀리다 describes losing your head because something has captured your attention. '뭐에 홀린 것 같다' is a common line when you did something strange without knowing why. 반하다 is about falling for someone, while 홀리다 feels more like being in a trance.

examples.en: The child buried his face in his dad's chest.

examples.ko: 가슴팍이 넓어서 그 셔츠가 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: He has a broad chest, so that shirt suits him well.
I spilled coffee and my whole chest got wet.
Try walking with your chest pushed out.
The T-shirt has a big logo on the chest.
The puppy jumped all the way up to my chest.

explain: '가슴'보다 겉에서 보이는 앞쪽 넓은 부분, 특히 옷이 닿는 부분을 말할 때 많이 써요. 마음이나 감정을 말할 때는 '가슴'을 쓰고 '가슴팍'은 쓰지 않아요. 주로 남자의 몸이나 옷 이야기에서 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: The child was held against his mother's chest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 앞가슴에 몸을 기댈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone leans into another person's chest.
phrases.en_equiv: to be held against the chest

phrases.en: He has broad shoulders and a broad chest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주로 남자의 체격을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to describe a man's build.

phrases.en: Coffee got on the chest of my shirt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷의 앞가슴 부분을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the chest area of clothing.

explain_en: Everyday word for the chest surface, as when hugging (아빠의 가슴팍) Compared with '가슴', it points to the broad front area of the body as seen from outside, especially where clothes sit. For feelings you use '가슴', not '가슴팍'. It is often heard when talking about a man's body or clothing.

t90.ax: Try walking with your chest pushed out.

en: to get shocked; to be electrically shocked

examples.ko: 젖은 손으로 전기 제품을 만지면 감전될 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you touch electrical products with wet hands, you can get shocked.

examples.ko: 공사장에서 일하던 사람이 감전돼서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: A worker at the construction site got an electric shock and went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 감전되는 사고는 비 오는 날에 더 위험해요.
examples.en: Electric shock accidents are more dangerous on rainy days.
I got shocked touching a broken outlet.

examples.ko: 아이가 감전되지 않게 콘센트를 가려 두세요.
examples.en: Cover the outlets so your child doesn't get shocked.

examples.ko: 전기 공사를 할 때는 감전될까 봐 늘 조심해요.
examples.en: I'm always careful about getting an electric shock when doing electrical work.

explain: 사고 뉴스와 안전 교육에서 많이 나와요. '감전되다'는 위험한 전기를 맞았을 때 쓰고, 겨울에 문고리에서 느끼는 따끔함은 '정전기가 일어나다'라고 해요. 형태가 피동이라 '전기에 감전되다'처럼 대상은 '에'로 말해요.

phrases.example: 비 오는 날에는 감전 사고가 나기 쉬워요.
phrases.en: Electric shock accidents happen easily on rainy days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스와 안전 교육에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in news and safety training.

phrases.en: Be careful so you don't get shocked.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주의를 줄 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form used when giving a warning.
phrases.en_equiv: so as not to be shocked

phrases.en: The risk of electric shock is high when there is water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain danger.

explain_en: Passive, very common — someone gets shocked by accident (전기 코드) It appears in accident news and safety training. 감전되다 is for a dangerous electric shock, while the small sting from a winter door handle is 정전기가 일어나다. The thing that shocks you takes 에, as in 전기에 감전되다.

t90.ax: I got shocked touching a broken outlet.

examples.ko: 운동을 하다가 골반이 아파서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: My pelvis hurt while exercising, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 오래 앉아 있으면 골반이 틀어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Sitting for a long time can throw your pelvis out of alignment.

examples.ko: 요가 선생님이 골반 스트레칭을 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The yoga teacher showed me a pelvis stretch.
I hurt my hip when I fell.

examples.ko: 의사가 골반 뼈 사진을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The doctor showed me an X-ray of my pelvic bone.
These pants fit snugly at the hips, so they are comfortable.

explain: 골반은 허리와 다리 사이를 받치는 뼈 전체예요. '엉덩이'는 그 겉에 있는 부분을 말해서 같은 말이 아니에요. 건강과 운동 이야기에서 골반이라고 하고, 옷 이야기에서는 '골반이 넓다'처럼 겉모습에도 써요.

phrases.example: 골반이 넓어서 바지가 잘 안 맞아요.
phrases.en: My hips are wide, so pants don't fit well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷 이야기에서는 겉모습을 말할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In talk about clothes, it also describes outward shape.

phrases.en: My pelvic pain was bad, so I rested.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건강 이야기에서 아픈 증상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in health talk to describe pain.

phrases.en: I stretch my pelvis before bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동 이야기에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in talk about exercise.

explain_en: 골반 is the whole bone structure that supports the body between the waist and the legs. '엉덩이' is the outer part, so they are not the same word. 골반 is used in health and exercise talk, and also for the outline of the body, as in '골반이 넓다' when talking about clothes.

examples.en: I fell on the stairs and broke my leg.
The doctor looked at the X-ray and said it was a fracture.

examples.ko: 골절 수술을 받고 한 달 동안 입원했어요.
examples.en: I had fracture surgery and stayed in the hospital for a month.
As you get older, the risk of fracture grows.
I broke my wrist while skiing.
It takes time for a fractured bone to heal.

explain: 병원에서 쓰는 말이에요. 일상에서는 '뼈가 부러지다'나 '다리가 부러졌다'고 훨씬 더 자주 말해요. 병원 안내나 뉴스에서는 '골절상'이라는 말도 나와요.

phrases.en: He suffered a fracture injury in a car accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뼈가 부러진 상처를 말하는 말로 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a broken-bone injury; common in the news.

phrases.en: I fell and broke my arm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '골절'보다 이 말을 훨씬 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life, people say this far more than 골절.

phrases.en: I had fracture surgery and stayed in the hospital for a week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 뼈를 고치는 수술을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for surgery to repair a broken bone.

explain_en: Medical term for a broken bone itself; the condition (다리 골절). A hospital word. In daily speech Koreans say 뼈가 부러지다 or 다리가 부러졌다 much more often. In hospital notices and the news you may also see 골절상.

t90.ax: I broke my wrist while skiing.

examples.ko: 공에 급소를 맞은 선수가 한참 일어나지 못했어요.
examples.en: The player hit by the ball in a vulnerable spot couldn't get up for a while.

examples.ko: 몸에는 세게 치면 위험한 급소가 있어요.
examples.en: The body has vital spots that are dangerous if hit hard.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 목은 다치면 위험한 급소라고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor said the neck is a vital spot that is dangerous to injure.

examples.ko: 발표 끝에 나온 질문이 우리 계획의 급소를 건드렸어요.
examples.en: A question at the end of the presentation touched the weak point of our plan.

examples.ko: 그 문제는 회사의 급소라서 말하기 조심스러워요.
examples.en: That issue is the company's sore spot, so I'm careful about mentioning it.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 급소만 콕 짚어서 말해요.
examples.en: That friend speaks by pinpointing only the crucial weak spots.

explain: 몸에서 다치면 크게 위험하거나 아픈 곳이에요. 비유로 일이나 사람의 가장 약한 부분, 핵심 약점을 가리킬 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 그의 한마디가 정확히 내 급소를 찔렀어요.
phrases.en: His one remark hit my weak spot exactly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 가장 아파하거나 감추고 싶은 약점을 정확히 건드릴 때 써요. 말이나 질문이 날카로울 때 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a remark or question touches exactly the point someone is most sensitive about or wants to hide.

explain_en: It is a spot on the body where an injury is especially dangerous or painful. Figuratively it also means the weakest, most crucial point of a matter or person.

examples.en: I fell and had my ankle put in a cast.
My leg was in a cast, so I couldn't go to school.
The doctor told me to put my arm in a cast.
Climbing stairs with a leg in a cast is hard.
How long do I have to wear the cast?
If your wrist is in a cast, writing is hard.

explain: '깁스를 하다'와 같은 뜻인데, 짧게 말할 때는 '깁스했어요'를 자주 써요. 다친 곳이 목적어로 와서 '다리를 깁스하다'처럼 말하고, 풀 때는 '깁스를 풀다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 뼈가 부러져서 한 달 동안 깁스해야 해요.
phrases.en: My bone is broken, so I have to wear a cast for a month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의사가 하라고 하거나 꼭 필요할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a doctor says so or when it is necessary.

phrases.en: It's hard to write with my arm in a cast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙는 모양이에요. 지금 깁스한 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form before a noun, describing the current state of wearing a cast.

phrases.en: I lived with a cast on for two months.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 지내다'를 붙여 깁스한 채로 보낸 시간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-go jinaeda' describes time spent with the cast on.
phrases.en_equiv: to get by with a cast on

explain_en: It means the same as '깁스를 하다', and the short form '깁스했어요' is common in speech. The injured part is the object, as in '다리를 깁스하다', and taking it off is '깁스를 풀다'.

examples.ko: 독극물은 아이 손이 닿지 않는 곳에 보관해야 해요.
examples.en: Poisons must be stored out of children's reach.

examples.ko: 공장에서 독극물이 새어 나와 마을이 위험해졌어요.
examples.en: Toxic substances leaked from the factory and the village is in danger.

examples.ko: 이 병에는 독극물 표시가 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: This bottle has a poison label on it.

examples.ko: 청소 용품 중에도 독극물에 가까운 것이 있어요.
examples.en: Some cleaning products are close to being poisonous.

examples.ko: 독극물을 마시면 바로 병원에 가야 해요.
examples.en: If you swallow poison, you must go to the hospital right away.
I was shocked by the news about a toxic substance accident.

explain: '독'은 몸에 해로운 성분이고, '독극물'은 그런 성분이 든 약품이나 물질이에요. '독약'은 사람을 해치는 약처럼 들려서 안전 안내나 뉴스에서는 '독극물'이나 '유독 물질'이라고 해요. 보통 '독극물 취급', '독극물 주의'처럼 나와요.

phrases.example: 독극물을 취급할 때는 장갑을 꼭 껴야 해요.
phrases.en: You must wear gloves when handling toxic substances.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안전 안내나 작업 규칙에서 '독극물을 다루는 일'을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in safety notices and work rules for handling toxic substances.

phrases.example: 독극물에 중독되면 바로 병원에 가야 해요.
phrases.en: If you are poisoned by a toxic substance, you must go to the hospital right away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 독극물을 잘못 먹거나 마셔서 몸이 아픈 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes getting sick after swallowing or breathing toxic substances.

phrases.example: 독극물 표시가 붙은 통은 만지지 마세요.
phrases.en: Don't touch containers with a poison label.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이나 통에 붙은 경고 표시를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to warning labels on bottles and containers.

explain_en: Broad term for poisonous materials; safety and legal contexts. '독' is a harmful component, and '독극물' is a chemical or substance containing it. '독약' sounds like medicine meant to harm people, so safety notices and news use '독극물' or '유독 물질'. It typically appears as '독극물 취급' or '독극물 주의'.

t90.ax: This bottle has a poison label on it.

en: being at one's feet; being underfoot

examples.en: Something caught under my feet and I almost fell.
The cat is sleeping at my feet.
Watch your step. The stairs are slippery.
The fallen leaves crunched underfoot.

examples.ko: 산 위에서 보니 구름이 발밑에 있었어요.
examples.en: From the mountaintop, the clouds were below my feet.
The ground shook beneath me and I thought it was an earthquake.

explain: 서 있는 자리의 바로 아래, 발이 닿는 곳을 말해요. '발아래'와 비슷하지만 '발밑'은 가까운 바닥에 쓰고, '발아래'는 높은 곳에서 내려다보는 풍경에 더 자주 써요. '발밑을 조심하다'는 안전 안내에 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: The stairs are slippery, so watch your step.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안전 안내에 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation, seen in safety warnings.

phrases.en: It's dark underfoot at night, so it's scary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바닥이 잘 안 보일 때 상태를 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state when the ground near your feet is hard to see.

phrases.example: 산 위에서 보니 도시가 발아래에 있어요.
phrases.en: From the top of the mountain, the city is below my feet.
phrases.nuance_ko: '발밑'은 가까운 바닥, '발아래'는 높은 곳에서 내려다보는 풍경에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '발밑' is the ground right at your feet; '발아래' is for a view looking down from high up.

explain_en: It means the spot right beneath where you stand. Similar to 발아래, but 발밑 is for the nearby ground, while 발아래 is more often for a view looking down from a height. 발밑을 조심하다 is common in safety notices.

examples.en: My skin got sunburned and it stings.
The cold wind touched my skin and I got goosebumps.
A baby's skin is really soft.
A mosquito bit my skin and it keeps itching.
My skin was chapped, so I put cream on it.

examples.ko: 뜨거운 물에 살갗을 데어서 많이 아파요.
examples.en: I burned my skin with hot water and it really hurts.

explain: '피부'보다 몸 겉에 닿는 느낌(바람, 햇볕, 아픔)을 말할 때 자주 어울려요. 그래서 '살갗이 따갑다', '살갗에 닿다'처럼 감각과 함께 많이 써요. '살가죽'보다 부드럽고 자연스러운 말이에요.

phrases.en: I fell and the skin on my knee got scraped off.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다쳐서 피부 겉이 벗겨질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the outer skin is scraped off by an injury.

phrases.en: The cold wind brushed against my skin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람이나 물건이 살짝 닿는 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the feeling of wind or an object lightly touching.

phrases.en: My skin stings when I get into salt water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상처나 피부가 따갑고 아플 때 쓰는 감각 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A sensation phrase for when skin or a wound stings.

explain_en: Compared with '피부', it fits well when you talk about what the body surface feels, such as wind, sun or pain. So you often see '살갗이 따갑다' or '살갗에 닿다'. It sounds softer and more natural than '살가죽'.

t90.ax: A baby's skin is really soft.

examples.en: I fell and broke my collarbone.
I was complimented on how nice my collarbone line looks.

examples.ko: 의사가 쇄골을 눌러 보고 아프냐고 물었어요.
examples.en: The doctor pressed on my collarbone and asked if it hurt.
The area between my shoulder and collarbone keeps feeling stiff.
The bag strap presses on my collarbone and it's uncomfortable.

examples.ko: 쇄골뼈는 가슴 위쪽에 가로로 길게 있어요.
examples.en: The collarbone runs long and horizontal across the upper chest.

explain: 병원 이야기와 몸매 이야기에서 많이 쓰고, 일상에서는 '쇄골뼈'라고도 해요. '쇄골이 부러지다', '쇄골이 드러나다'처럼 써요. '어깨', '목'은 훨씬 넓은 부분을 가리켜서 쇄골과 달라요.

phrases.en: My collarbone hurt, so I went to the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '쇄골뼈'라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday speech people also say '쇄골뼈'.

phrases.en: When you wear this top, your collarbones show.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷이나 몸매 이야기에서 보이는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes visibility in talk about clothes or body shape.

phrases.en: I hurt my collarbone while playing soccer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고나 운동 중에 다친 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for injuries from accidents or sports.

explain_en: It shows up in medical talk and in talk about body shape, and people also say '쇄골뼈'. Common combinations are '쇄골이 부러지다' (the collarbone breaks) and '쇄골이 드러나다' (the collarbone shows). '어깨' and '목' cover a much wider area than 쇄골.
